newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Greens to protest at plutonium ship.
newsitem.headline: S.African Greens to protest at plutonium ship.

text.p: Environmental groups urged South Africa on Friday to bar a ship carrying radioactive nuclear waste from rounding the Cape, but the government said it was satisfied the shipment was safe.

"If the ship were to have an accident it would contaminate our marine life. We therefore urge the Minister of Environmental Affairs (Pallo Jordan) to ban the route of the ship," Cecelia Assad, spokeswoman for the Green Coalition Anti-Nuclear Group, said in a telephone interview.

"If the government does not comply with our request we are planning public demonstrations from next week... these companies are taking the route thinking because we are a third world country we won't make a noise," she said.
A British ship, the Pacific Teal, is carrying the waste to Japan from France where it has been reprocessed. It is expected to pass South Africa in mid-February.

The Department of Environmental Affairs said it accepted assurances from those involved in the shipment that there was no threat to public health and that the ship would not come closer than about 120 miles to the coast.
"The reason we feel confident... is based on an extensive range of safety measures that have been put in place around the shipment," department spokeswoman Cassandra Gabriel said.
She said the vessel would be monitored on a 24-hour basis by a team of nuclear experts and that there were comprehensive emergency plans meant to deal with any eventuality.
A total of 30 shipments of this kind have been scheduled.
